note: North end of Hanlan's Point, where the airport is: cottages, the amusement park and the stadium. Removed for the airport, 1937-38 (island.csv rows hanlans_point, amusement_park, stadium, airport). The park and stadium burned in 1909 and were rebuilt for 1910, so their buildings on the 1913 plan are really of 1910; they get the same spread as the cottages.
Rest of Hanlan's Point: Metro Parks clearance from 1956, remaining houses demolished spring 1962 (island.csv, hanlans_point).

Centre Island: homes from 1880; clearance from 1956; Manitou Road gone by 1959. No source gives an end year for Centre Island alone; 1968 is my reading of 'about 370 homes left by 1963, about 100 more removed later' and 'all remaining homes on Ward's and Algonquin by 1970' (island.csv, centre_island).
Ward's and Algonquin: the community survives, so no lost buildings are drawn here; today's houses are shown with their own years.

name: Trinity College (original building)
note: Built 1851 on Queen Street West to Kivas Tully's design, opened January 1852; the college moved to Hoskin Avenue in 1925 and the grounds became Trinity Bellwoods Park (Wikipedia, Trinity College). Demolition: 1956-57 as supplied by Andreas; Wikipedia says 'in the 1950s' (Trinity College) and 'most were demolished in the early 1950s' (Trinity Bellwoods Park). Every outline the plans show inside the box gets these years, so later wings are dated too early. The height (14 m) is assumed; the towers are not modelled.
